Glenn Gibbins, who was voted on to Sunderland council in May, wrote on Facebook in March 2024: “Carnt believe the amount of nigerians in town … should melt them all down and fill in the pot holes!!” Continue reading... item.title: Iran was behind cyber-attack on French supermarket freezers, Paris says
item.description: French foreign minister vows European sanctions against Tehran over ‘unprecedented’ hacks last month France has said Iran was responsible for a massive cyber-attack on supermarket freezers and chiller cabinets that was described by its foreign minister as being an act of “unprecedented scale and unprecedented aggression”. Jean-Noël Barrot said “Europe-wide sanctions” would be imposed against those responsible, adding that the attacks – which took control of digital thermostats to push temperatures up to above 50C – constituted “a major violation of the nation’s interests”. item.title: Air pollution soars as fog traps emissions in England’s urban areas
item.description: Particles from fireworks and bonfires likely to have contributed to levels well above WHO’s daily guideline Air pollution soared to “very high” levels across urban parts of England on Monday as still, foggy weather kept emissions trapped after a weekend of fireworks and bonfires. Government monitoring showed 11 sites, mainly in London and Greater Manchester, reached the highest band on its 10-point index for particulate matter in the 24 hours to 10am. A further 27 sites recorded “high” levels across the capital, the north-west, the Midlands, Yorkshire and the east of England. Continue… Publicado también por: The Guardian - Environment. item.description: An Oregon couple in their 70s have been awarded more than $8 million after a jury found companies liable for unlawfully foreclosing on their home while they were still living in it. The Salem couple had also been denied more than $175,000 left over from the foreclosure sale, which took place in 2022. The jury found that the companies had carried out unlawful trade practices and financially abused the elderly homeowners. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Meet Leo Toake, 16, who turned potato peels into weedkiller and restored 15 acres in New Jersey
item.description: At just 16 years old, Leo Toake from New Jersey is on a mission to create a revolutionary herbicide sourced from food scraps. Through his nonprofit, Re:Imagine Inc., he's mobilized over 70 volunteers for habitat restoration and invasive species removal. Early trials of Toake's S.A.F.E. clearly show an 82.5% effectiveness against Japanese stilt grass, all while repurposing over 500 pounds of food waste and contributing to a cleaner environment.
